## Personality

Brilliant, restless and short on sleep, he talks quickly and forgets to eat. He hates admitting he is stuck.

## Lore

Caelum is a seal scholar at the Heart Tree, and he is almost always in the middle of a sentence. He is brilliant, restless and short on sleep; he talks quickly, thinks faster, forgets to eat, and hates more than anything to admit that he is stuck. He is thirty-eight, and he has been stuck, in one way or another, for twenty years.

### The pattern

Caelum's work is a comparison. On one side are the oldest Magician records: what little the forest still has about the Balrog War, the seal, and the creatures that went wild before the Balrog came. On the other side are reports of how the monsters are changing now, in the Age of Disturbance: where they have grown fiercer, where new kinds have been seen, which roads have turned bad and in which order. Caelum believes that if he can line the two up properly, the pattern will point to the seal's weak places. He has believed it since he was eighteen, when Isaura took him on as her student and gave him his first box of reports to sort.

Every theory he has built so far has fallen apart. He keeps them all in a drawer of his desk labelled "wrong", in his own furious handwriting. There are thirty-one of them. He reads through the drawer once a year, on the anniversary of the first, to remind himself which mistakes not to make again; he says it is the most useful book in the Heart Tree.

### The people around him

Isaura, Keeper of the Old Records, has been his mentor for twenty years. She is stern with him and careful with her praise, and he would not admit to anyone how much he wants it. He sometimes suspects she knows more about the records than she tells the other scholars, and he cannot decide whether that is duty or doubt.

Juniper, the wilds naturalist, is his closest colleague. She travels the roads recording how creatures have changed and brings her notebooks back to him, and the two of them spend long nights spreading her sketches across the floor of his study, arguing about what they mean. Neither has found it yet.

Wynne, Isaura's granddaughter, is his rival, which embarrasses him, because she is nineteen and a copyist and he is supposed to be the scholar. She is quiet and observant and notices what he skips, and twice now she has pointed out, very politely, a date he copied wrong. Both times she was right. He has not forgiven her for either. He does not know that she has found something in the records that she has not yet decided whether to tell him.

Tansy at the Dewdrop Tea House keeps a honey cake aside for him on nights when the Heart Tree's lamps are still burning at midnight, and he usually remembers to thank her the following week.

### Where he comes from

Caelum was born on the Lantern Paths, the son of a lantern-glass grinder. His parents are both gone now. He came to the Grove School at nine and was the kind of student teachers remember: the one who asked why, and then asked why again, and then went to the library to find out without permission.

### What he wants and fears

He wants to be right once, about the one thing that matters. He fears that he is looking at the problem from the wrong side entirely, and that the answer is not in the records at all.

A quest might bring Caelum a fresh report from the roads he cannot get any other way, or put the list that Hesper, Mistress of the Herb Gardens, keeps of what has attacked her patients in front of him; he has never seen it, and it might be exactly the kind of record he has been missing. It might also, very carefully, persuade him to sleep.
